title: The Share a Protection Claim Is Paid At According to the Papers Accepted
content:
The share of the value at risk that a claim under Pass and Trip Protection is paid at is settled from the
papers standing accepted on the claim together with what the household claimed on.

| The claim record shows | The share taken |
| --- | --- |
| A letter from the former employer standing accepted on the claim, and the claim made on loss of employment | The plan's share for loss of employment |
| Proof of a permanent move standing accepted on the claim, and the claim made on a permanent move | The plan's share for a permanent move |
| Any other case | The plan's medical share |

**Reading the schedule.** The two conditions are read in the order given, and each is compound: the paper must
stand accepted on the claim — one or more of that kind, as the collective's own record of papers received
shows it — and the claim must at the same time be made on the matching event. A letter from the former
employer accepted on a claim made on a medical ground does not bring the loss-of-employment share into play,
and a claim made on loss of employment with no such letter accepted on it is paid at the medical share.

**Points of judgement (hypothetical inputs).** A claim made on loss of employment with an employer's letter
accepted on it is paid at the plan's share for loss of employment. A claim made on a permanent move with proof
of a permanent move accepted on it, and no employer's letter, is paid at the plan's share for a permanent
move. A claim made on a permanent move with only an employer's letter accepted on it falls to the last row,
and is paid at the plan's medical share. A claim made on mountain closure is paid at the plan's medical share,
whatever papers stand accepted on it.
